summary_paraphrase: A sea anemone stuck to one rock feels lonely and different from every creature that can swim or walk. When a hermit crab is chased by a big fish she shields him with her stings; he wants her courage, she wants his adventures, and by making her laugh off her rock he carries her away on his shell, where she guards him and is never lonely again.

beats.function: a fixed creature, content but prickly
envy turns into a cry for help
she faces down the bully fish
mutual envy, then laughter frees her
adventures together, stings used to protect
never lonely: answers the problem line

characters.name: Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee
characters.problem: she is fixed to one rock and has no legs or fins
characters.change: from lonely and prickly to a protector with a friend
characters.humor_source: her grumpy face while being praised

characters.name: Herman
characters.desire: safety, a bodyguard; to be brave
characters.fear: the fish that wants to pull him from his shell
characters.change: from hunted hermit to travelling partner
characters.relation_to_protagonist: rescued stranger who becomes her friend and carrier

characters.name: the big fish
characters.humor_source: cheeky flick of the tail as he leaves

humor_notes: Humor arrives late and physically: Herman's dance and faces make her laugh so hard she pops off her rock. A smaller joke sits in the picture on page 7: she still frowns while being called brave.

repetition.description: Her stinging tentacles return three times: first to drive others away, then to defend Herman, finally only to protect him
repetition.why: the same trait changes meaning, which carries the character change without stating a moral

repetition.description: Parallel lament of what she lacks ('no fins', 'no feet') and a later mirrored exchange where each says what they lack and wish for
repetition.why: the mirror between her wish and Herman's sets up the shared solution

repetition.description: The loneliness word from the problem returns in the last line; 'tasty treats' returns from the opening
repetition.why: closes the circle on the stated problem

notes: Page 3 (one short line) relies on scale: a crowded reef with her as a tiny figure at the edge.
The predator enters as a jaw in the corner on page 5 before it fills page 6.
On page 7 the picture keeps her cross face while the text praises her bravery.
Pages 10-12 switch to white backgrounds and round vignettes: the montage of adventures on page 11 lives only in the pictures.

strengths: the trait that isolates her (stings) becomes the gift she offers, shown not stated
a mutual-need friendship: each has what the other lacks
the closing line answers the opening problem word
a clear danger beat in the middle with a fast, non-violent resolution
weaknesses: sentences run long for a picture book (longest 19 words; page 7 holds 50 words)
the jump from 'stuck' to 'popped off by laughing' is a magical shortcut not set up earlier

age_suitability.notes: Brief peril: a toothy fish wants to pull the crab from its shell; resolved without harm. The word 'bully' and stinging as defence are mild.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address
